issues.title: Persistent USE-keyspace failure breaks the pool instead of base's warn+keep
issues.verdictReason: handle_ready_connection's new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm (connection_pool.rs:900-909) discards the connection and, once is_filling()/is_empty() hold, calls update_shared_conns(Some(err.into())), which sets MaybePoolConnections::Broken and fires a Lost event (update_shared_conns, ~line 1128-1188); each subsequent refill repeats the same failing USE since current_keyspace is never cleared, so a node with a persistently failing keyspace stays Broken forever. In the base, the same failure (diff hunk removing the old start_setting_keyspace_for_connection body) only logged warn! and still returned Ok((connection, error_receiver)), keeping the node usable for fully-qualified queries.
issues.scopeReason: The discard-on-keyspace-failure behavior is new code added by commit 7f48315d in this PR.

issues.title: New UseKeyspaceError-to-ConnectionError mapping violates ConnectionError's own contract
issues.verdictReason: ConnectionError is documented as indicating 'connection can no longer be used and should be dropped' (errors.rs:568-570), but the new UseKeyspaceError(#[from] UseKeyspaceError) variant is produced for UseKeyspaceError::RequestError (server rejection), ::KeyspaceNameMismatch, and ::RequestTimeout (errors.rs:183-208) -- none of which mean the connection itself is broken -- and this is the sole producer feeding I1's Broken-pool path. The resulting message also only interpolates UseKeyspaceError's own Display, which for RequestTimeout/KeyspaceNameMismatch/RequestError never includes the keyspace name being set.
issues.scopeReason: The ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant and its mapping are new in this PR.

issues.title: total_connections gauge leaks on shard-aware excess rejection and on pool teardown
issues.verdictReason: When a shard-aware connection is rejected because the target shard is already full (the `else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()` branch at connection_pool.rs:994-1006), the connection is dropped without ever being added to conns or excess_connections and without a matching dec_total_connections call, even though count_in_metrics already incremented the gauge on open (line ~1046).
